policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'and its branches became long' renders the lemma as a plural possessed noun, but the ketiv פארתו is only a defective consonantal spelling of the same word and admits the identical plural reading, so the English wording cannot distinguish the two. The one mapped note ('Or, great') is classed alternative_rendering and concerns English wording, not the reading; there is no italicized supply bearing on it. Both candidates remain compatible and the qere base fallback carries the projection.
